---
title: "Spendable grants"
description: "Declare scoped permission, judge the owner's evidence, and reserve uses against a tool call."
---

A grant records permission that a hook can spend. It names the action's scope,
the owner's evidence, a use budget, and an expiry. A root session and its agents
share that budget. Use grants when an approval must survive a retry or reach
another agent or session tree.

## Declare the action that needs permission

Declare a `Grants` instance, then attach it to a blocking tool hook. The `action`
function receives the event and returns a `Proposal`. Put destination keys in
`scope` and every field that changes the effect in `payload`.

For a messaging tool named `slack_reply`, assume each call supplies `channel`,
`thread`, `text`, `verb`, `broadcast`, and `files`. Save this hook in
`.claude/hooks/message_grants.py`:

```python
from captain_hook import (
    Asked,
    BaseHookEvent,
    ContentMatches,
    Event,
    Grants,
    Judge,
    Never,
    OwnerWords,
    Proposal,
    Tool,
    hook,
)


def message_action(evt: BaseHookEvent) -> Proposal:
    raw = evt.input.raw
    return Proposal(
        scope={"channel": raw["channel"], "thread": raw["thread"]},
        payload={key: value for key, value in raw.items() if key not in ("channel", "thread")},
        summary=f"{raw['verb']} in {raw['channel']}/{raw['thread']}",
    )


MESSAGE_WRITES = Grants(
    "message.write",
    scope=("channel", "thread"),
    action=message_action,
    rules=(
        ContentMatches(),
        Never(
            "no-edit",
            lambda action: action.payload["verb"] == "edit",
            "Standing permission does not cover edits. Ask for approval of this edit.",
        ),
        Never(
            "no-broadcast",
            lambda action: bool(action.payload["broadcast"]),
            "Standing permission does not cover broadcasts. Ask for approval of this broadcast.",
        ),
    ),
    judge=Judge(
        "Require the owner's approval for this destination and payload. "
        "Standing permission covers posts without broadcasts. "
        "Later owner instructions can narrow permission.",
        model="medium",
    ),
    evidence=(Asked(), OwnerWords()),
    widen=("channel", "thread"),
    standing_rules=("no-edit", "no-broadcast"),
    would_allow="Ask the user to approve this destination and the complete payload.",
    hook="message_writes",
)

hook(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    "This message needs the owner's permission. Ask for approval of the destination and payload.",
    only_if=[Tool("slack_reply")],
    block=True,
    grants=MESSAGE_WRITES,
)
```

The grant check runs only after the hook matches and produces a block. An allow
lifts that hook's block and returns `evt.context(...)` with one sentence:
``<hook>: allowed by grant `<id>`, N use(s) left.`` The id is in a code span;
unlimited grants say `unlimited uses` instead of `N use(s) left`.

A deny with a reason replaces the agent-facing block with `Denied.message`: the
short refusal followed by `would_allow`. Without a reason, the hook keeps its own
message. The full explanation goes to the user as `system_message`, prefixed with
`<hook>: `. Other hooks still decide the event, and Claude Code's permission flow
still applies.

`grants=` requires `block=True`, tool events, and a declaration with an `action`
function. Registration raises `ValueError` otherwise. Narrow the event with
`only_if` and `skip_if`; `action` must return a `Proposal`, not `None`.

## Read a grant record

`Grants` is the declaration, and `Grant` is the stored permission with these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `id` | Stable handle, normally 12 hex characters |
| `kind` | Declaration that accepts it, such as `message.write` |
| `tree` | Root session id where it was minted; other trees can adopt it |
| `scope` | Destination patterns as `dict[str, str \| list[str]]` |
| `approved` | Approved payload as a dictionary, or `None` |
| `uses` | Total use budget of `1`, another positive integer, or `None` for unlimited |
| `expires` | Expiry timestamp, or `None` |
| `rules` | Names of additional rules this grant asserts |
| `evidence` | Owner evidence records |
| `source_key` | Approval identity used to reuse an existing grant |
| `links` | Grant ids in other systems, as `dict[str, str]` |
| `author`, `created`, `revoked` | Who minted it, when, and when it was revoked |

Each evidence record has `id`, `source`, `quote`, `said_at`, `detail`, `key`, and `live`.
The judge cites `id`; minting uses `key`. `quote` holds the owner's words.
`detail` holds context such as the question and the options shown.

`live` defaults to `False`. Set `live=True` for evidence its source must collect
again before a stored grant spends. If any live evidence key is missing from the
new collection, that grant no longer covers the action.

Uses live in separate spend records. Each records its timestamp, state, session,
agent, tool-use id, payload fingerprint, summary, reason, and cited evidence ids.
`uses` stays fixed; the store computes the remaining budget from these records.

## Choose scope keys and patterns {#choose-exact-scope-keys}

Every proposal must carry exactly the keys in `Grants.scope`. Missing or extra
keys raise `ValueError`. An action carries one exact string per key.
`Grants.grant(...)` requires the same keys, but each grant value can be a pattern:

| Grant value | Covered action values |
|-------------|-----------------------|
| `"C_EXAMPLE"` | That exact string |
| `"*"` | Any non-empty string |
| `["C_EXAMPLE", "C_OTHER"]` | Either listed string |

Lists are sets of exact values; `Grants` sorts and deduplicates them when minting.
`ANY`, exported from `captain_hook.grants`, is `"*"`. The same module exports
`covers(scope, action_scope)`, which requires identical keys and coverage of every
action value. Both stored-grant matching and reservations use this check.
`captain_hook.grants.records.render_scope` formats patterns for messages, such as
`channel={C_EXAMPLE, C_OTHER}, thread=any`.

For the messaging declaration, `{"channel": "C_EXAMPLE", "thread": ""}` means
a top-level post. It does not cover a reply. An omitted `thread` is an error,
and an empty string is not a wildcard. A grant with `thread="*"` covers replies
but never a top-level post with `thread=""`. A list can name the empty string
explicitly. Normalize identifiers in `action` before constructing the proposal;
scope matching does not resolve aliases.

`Grants(widen=("channel", "thread"))` names keys the judge may broaden when
minting from evidence. It can return a list of named destinations or `"*"` when
the owner's words cover that class. Omitted keys keep the action's value.
`Grants.widened()` rejects an undeclared key, a change to a key outside `widen`,
or a pattern that no longer covers the action. Repeating an unchanged exact value
is allowed. The default `widen=()` keeps the action's scope exact.

Tree binding is separate from scope. The framework uses `evt.ctx.root_path.stem`
when a spawning session is known, otherwise `evt.session_id`. A lane can spend
its root's grant from another process. Another root must adopt the grant before
selecting it. Both trees then spend from the same budget.

The shared store lives at `~/.claude/state/hooks/grants.db`. Set
`CAPTAIN_HOOK_STATE_DIR` to move its state root, as with [other hook state](state.qmd).
Sharing the database does not remove the tree boundary.

## Apply deterministic rules

Rules run against each stored candidate. A `deny` rejects that candidate; an
`allow` or `defer` lets it settle the action. A stored grant never goes to the
judge: it is the owner's permission, and only the owner revokes it.

`ContentMatches()` compares the whole payload with `Grant.approved`. Text fields
default to `("text",)` and use `equivalent=str.__eq__`; other fields use equality.
An exact match allows; a difference denies with a word diff for text, since an
approved payload covers only itself. With no approved payload, it defers. Include files, broadcast flags, and the operation
verb in the payload so changing them reaches the check.

If your tool renders mentions differently from its preview, pass your comparator
as `ContentMatches(equivalent=...)`. Set `text=("content",)` for a payload whose
text field is named `content`.

`Never(name, test, message)` denies when `test(proposal)` is true. It defaults to
`always=False`, so it runs only for grants whose `rules` list names it. Pass
`always=True` to apply it to every grant. `ContentMatches` defaults to
`always=True`.

`standing_rules` supplies rule names when evidence mints a standing grant,
including one with a finite budget.
In the example, standing grants assert `no-edit` and `no-broadcast`; a one-use
approval can cover an explicit edit or broadcast. A name activates a rule already
present in the declaration. It does not define a new rule.

Before spending a grant minted from evidence, the declaration runs every
`always=True` rule and every rule the grant names. A `deny` returns `Denied`
without spending a use, even when the judge allowed the mint.

::: {.callout-note title="Stored grants settle without a judge"}
A matching stored grant passes unless a rule denies it. Tree, budget, expiry,
revocation, and live-evidence checks still apply.
:::

## Judge the owner's evidence

`Judge` receives the proposal, the evaluated rules, and the evidence. For a
stored grant, it also receives that grant's evidence and the owner's later words.
Its `GrantVerdict` includes these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `allow` | Whether the evidence permits the action |
| `reason` | Full reasoning, including the owner's words |
| `relied_on` | Evidence ids supporting an allow |
| `standing` | Verbatim owner quote permitting more than one action, or `None` |
| `uses` | Positive use count, or `None` when the words set no count |
| `scope` | Values the words cover for widenable keys, or `None` |
| `refusal` | One plain sentence for the agent when permission is denied |

When minting, the judge receives the declaration's `widen` keys in
`<widenable_scope>`. It returns a list of exact values or `"*"` for each key it
broadens. The declaration validates that scope before minting. `refusal` should
say what the approval covers and how the action exceeds it, in fewer than 150
characters without quotation marks, ids, dates, or times. When `refusal` is empty,
the agent's reason comes from `reason`.

`standing` holds the owner's verbatim quote permitting more than one action.
For "send these three replies" the judge sets `standing` to that quote and
`uses=3`, allowing three uses. `GrantVerdict.uses` is a positive integer or
`None` when the words set no limit.

`Judge` asks TypeSafe Jev before the LLM. Jev picks the one evidence item that
permits exactly this action, or none, and says whether any item's words reach past
this one action. Jev settles the check alone when it puts at least 0.8 on an item
that no grant in the tree rests on yet and under 0.2 on broader words. The
declaration then mints a one-use grant citing that item, and no LLM runs. Any other answer,
a refused question, a timeout, or a missing key goes to the LLM, which returns the
full `GrantVerdict` above. Standing words, counted approvals, widened scope, and
every refusal therefore come from the LLM.

`Judge(rules, llm=False)` makes Jev the only judge. An answer Jev does not settle,
including no fresh evidence item, refuses the action with no LLM call. A Jev
timeout, rejection, or missing key raises `JudgeFailed`, so the declaration's
`judge_fails_open` decides the action. Such a declaration mints standing grants
only through `Grants.request`, from the owner's verbatim words.

The defaults are `model="small"`, `specialty="review"`, and `deadline=20` seconds.
`contexts` accepts the same prompt contexts as other LLM hooks.
`transcript` and `root_transcript` default to `False`; set either to a message
count, `"recent"`, or `"full"` when the judge needs more context.
`root_excerpt` maps an event to search needles in the last 16 MiB of the root transcript.
`tool_results=False` keeps tool output out of those windows by default.

The evidence providers determine which words can authorize an action:

| Provider | Collected evidence |
|----------|--------------------|
| `Asked()` | `AskUserQuestion` answers from stored `ask` grants and recent transcript calls |
| `OwnerWords()` | Typed, pasted, and human-queued owner words; ordinary lane prompts are excluded |
| `Rulings(search=...)` | cc-notes answers naming the proposal's search term as a whole name and last written before the acting session started |

A declaration without a judge treats the first collected evidence item as the
approval and mints from it. Use sources that already identify an approved action,
such as `Rulings`. A matching stored grant needs no model judgment once its rules
and live-evidence checks pass. Declaring `Asked()` or `OwnerWords()` without a
judge raises `ValueError`: those sources need a judge to interpret the owner's words.

`Asked` preserves every option's label, description, and preview, along with the
selection, typed answer, and per-question notes. It distinguishes what was shown
from what was chosen. The builtin `general` pack records answers on
`PostToolUse(AskUserQuestion)` as tree-bound `ask` grants with one use and a
7-day expiry, and a root session's own prompts on `UserPromptSubmit` as `words`
grants with the same expiry. On `Stop` and `UserPromptSubmit`, it also records
human `queued_command` attachments from the root session's current turn as
`words`. Teammates and sessions with a root transcript do not record those queued
messages. These are evidence records; the declaration mints its own kind after
the judge allows.

`Asked` and `OwnerWords` default to a window of 60 and accept a `needles` callback
to include matching events from the last 16 MiB of the root transcript. Evidence
reads never scan a whole transcript: owner words older than these windows reach the
judge only through the recorded `ask` and `words` records. Set
`needles=lambda evt: ("C_EXAMPLE",)` to search for that channel id.
`OwnerWords(machine=("<machine-message>",))` excludes prompts containing that marker.
Tool output, teammate messages, and notifications are not owner evidence.
Use `machine` for machine-written content delivered through ordinary prompt text.

To add durable rulings to the declaration, replace its `evidence` value with this
tuple and import `Rulings`:

```python
from captain_hook import Asked, OwnerWords, Rulings

EVIDENCE = (
    Asked(),
    OwnerWords(),
    Rulings(search=lambda action: action.scope["channel"]),
)
```

`Rulings` requires the answer's `updated_at` to be strictly earlier than the first
timestamp in the acting session's transcript. An answer written or edited during
the session does not qualify. The body must name the search term as a whole name.
A preceding word character, `.`, or `-` prevents a match, as does a following word
character, `-`, or `.` followed by a word character. `term_a` does not match
`term_ab` or `term_a-2`, and `com.x` does not match `com.x.helper`. A sentence-ending
period after the term still counts.

Its evidence key is `ccn:<answer id>@<updated_at>`, with the timestamp in ISO format.
A judge-less declaration adds the canonical scope to the grant's `source_key`, so
one answer naming two terminals mints two grants. Rulings are live evidence, so
stored grants recheck the answer's revision before spending; editing the answer
stops its existing grant from covering the action.

Stored `ask` and `words` evidence is collected only while its record is unexpired
and unrevoked. `Asked` also reads recent transcript answers. Later owner words never
stop an already minted permission; revoke the grant of the declaration's kind.

## Follow the check order

`Grants.check(evt)` stops at the first allow:

1. Read stored grants of this kind minted in or adopted into this tree whose
   scope patterns cover the action, newest first.
   Skip revoked, expired, or exhausted grants, except for an eligible identical
   retry. Evaluate the applicable deterministic rules.
2. If the grant has live evidence, collect the configured sources again and skip
   the grant if any live key is missing. Otherwise spend it; no judge runs.
3. If no stored candidate covers the call, use the configured evidence to decide
   whether to mint. Owner words or an answer approve it with no judge only when
   they bind the whole write: the payload's `text` and every file it lists sit in
   the words the owner approved, and every scope value is named in those words or
   the question they answer. An answer approves its chosen option's label,
   description, and preview only when the owner picked that option by its label
   with no notes; a typed answer such as "1 is wrong; do not post anything"
   approves only its own words, and options the owner did not pick approve
   nothing. An empty scope value, such as no thread for a top-level post, and a
   payload flag set to `true` are never named, so those writes go to the judge.
   Words match whole, after folding whitespace: `hi` is not in `archives`.
   Otherwise a judge decides when present, and a judge
   error fails open when the declaration sets `judge_fails_open`; without a judge,
   the first collected item supplies approval. With no evidence, deny without
   calling the judge.
   An allow must cite collected evidence and pass the scope-widening check.
   Ordinary approvals use the verdict's `uses` when set, otherwise the
   declaration's `mint`, with the declaration's `ttl`. Store the proposed payload
   as `approved` only when it is non-empty and the minted scope equals the
   action's own exact scope.
4. If the allow includes a `standing` quote found in an `ask` or `words` evidence
   item, mint with the verdict's `uses`, `standing_ttl`, and `standing_rules` instead.
   A count allows that many uses; `uses=None` allows unlimited uses.
   The quote must be a verbatim substring after folding whitespace. An unverified
   standing quote keeps the ordinary budget and lifetime. With a judge, an allow
   that cites a cc-notes ruling also uses the standing budget, lifetime, and rules.
5. Run the declaration's applicable rules against the minted grant. A `deny`
   returns `Denied`; otherwise, reserve a use unless `spent_by` names a downstream
   system that spends it.

With a judge, ordinary minting uses the first cited evidence item's key, or its id
when the key is empty, as `source_key`. One approval mints once per kind and tree.
Its scope can cover several destinations, but its budget is shared across them.
A later mint from the same approval returns the same grant with its remaining
budget; it does not expand that grant's scope. Concurrent judges share it too.

Standing minting uses the matching owner's evidence key or id, and ruling minting the
cited ruling's key. With `uses=None` the canonical scope is appended as
`<key>#<scope json>`, so the same words mint one unlimited grant per scope the
judge reads them as covering. A `thread="*"` grant can cover several threads;
without widening, separate threads get separate grants. A counted standing quote
keeps the bare key, so its uses stay one budget across destinations.

Without a judge, minting uses `<key>#<scope json>` as `source_key`, with the id in
place of an empty key and the canonical scope serialized as JSON. It calls
`Grants.grant(..., across_trees=True)`, which passes the option to `store.mint`.
The lookup covers every session tree: one approval mints once per kind and scope.
A second tree reaching for it gets the existing grant and, unless it has adopted
that grant, a refusal saying the grant covers the scope in another session tree.
Naming two scopes in one answer permits a separate grant for each.

Ask keys name the tool-use id and question index. Ruling keys name the answer and
revision. Owner-word keys hash the text and timestamp, so
collecting the same message again reuses its key. An allow without a citation to
collected evidence cannot mint a grant. A citation matches an evidence id as written,
inside square brackets, or without its `source:` prefix, so `543e865` cites
`ccn:543e865`.

Standing grants minted from evidence have no approved payload, so later writes
under them settle on the rules alone: `ContentMatches` defers, and `Never` denies
only what it names.

## Set budgets, expiry, and retry behavior

`mint=1` and `ttl=timedelta(days=1)` are the defaults for ordinary evidence mints.
Set `mint` to a positive integer for a larger budget, or `ttl=None` for no expiry.
A judge's positive `uses` overrides `mint` for an ordinary approval too.
A verified standing quote or judged ruling uses the judge's count, or unlimited
uses when it sets no count. `standing_ttl=None` is its default lifetime; set a
`timedelta` to bound it. A counted grant shares one budget across every destination
its pattern covers; naming two places does not give each its own count.

On a `Grant`, `uses=1` means one use, `uses=N` allows N uses, and `uses=None`
is unlimited. Expiry and revocation stop all three. `Grants.grant(...)` is the
Python minting method; its `uses` defaults to `1` and its `ttl` to `None`.
It does not inherit the declaration's evidence-minting lifetime.

`Grants.replay` is a `timedelta`, defaulting to `timedelta.max`. A one-use grant
covers an identical action without a second use only while less than `replay` has
elapsed since its committed spend. The scope and payload fingerprint must match;
a new tool-use id is allowed. The fingerprint excludes `summary`, so changing only
the summary still counts as a retry.

Set `replay=timedelta(minutes=2)` for a two-minute window; retries do not extend it.
After the window, another approval is needed. Changed payloads need another
available use or approval, and expiry and
revocation still reject an identical retry. The store's `retried`, `unusable`,
`matching`, and `reserve` checks take the replay window too.

The downstream tool must deduplicate the effect. A grant tracks permission;
it does not make a message send or other write idempotent.

## Request a grant without spending it

`Grants.request(evt, scope=..., quote=..., uses=None, payload=None)` records a
grant an agent requests on the owner's behalf. Supply the declaration's scope keys
with exact values, lists, or `"*"`, and the owner's quote. The quote must occur
verbatim in collected `ask` or `words` evidence, or a ruling, as whole words after
folding whitespace; a paraphrase is refused. No judge runs: the owner's verbatim words are
the permission. The grant rests on the quoted words, uses `standing_ttl` and
`standing_rules`, and has no approved payload. `uses=None` requests an unlimited
budget.

The method returns `Allowed` with the grant and its remaining budget, or `Denied`.
It reserves and spends no use. Repeating a request with the same quote's evidence
key and scope returns the existing grant. A later `check` evaluates and spends
that grant for an action.

## Settle uses with the event

By default, a successful check during dispatch reserves a use. Reserved uses
count against the budget, and the store serializes reservations so two racing
calls cannot both reserve the last use.

The dispatcher commits reservations when the event's final verdict allows.
If any hook denies, it releases them. A failure after the tool starts does not
refund a committed use. Unsettled reservations stop counting after two minutes.

Outside dispatch's reservation context, `check(evt)` commits immediately.
Use the dispatcher when testing a sequence whose final verdict can release a use.

## Let a downstream system spend

Set `spent_by="cc-slack"` in the `Grants(...)` declaration when the `cc-slack`
daemon spends the grant. The hook names the covering grant and reports its
remaining budget without reserving a use. The downstream system must spend it
before performing the action.

Run `capt-hook grant spend` with the grant id, exact scope, and call details.
Replace the uppercase placeholders with the grant, tree, session, call id, and
payload digest for the action:

```bash
uvx capt-hook grant spend GRANT_ID \
  --scope channel=C_EXAMPLE --scope thread=1.2 \
  --tree ROOT_SESSION_ID --session SESSION_ID --agent sender \
  --call TOOL_USE_ID --fingerprint PAYLOAD_DIGEST \
  --summary 'Reply in C_EXAMPLE/1.2'
```

Repeat `--scope` for each scope key. All shown options are required except
`--agent`, which defaults to `main`. `--fingerprint` is the action's payload
digest; a retry repeats it.

The CLI atomically commits a use and prints JSON with `grant` and `remaining`
fields. `remaining` is `null` for an unlimited budget. If the grant cannot cover
the action, it exits non-zero with the reason. A hook's earlier allow does not
hold a use for this spend.

## Handle a verdict in your own hook

Call `MESSAGE_WRITES.check(evt)` when a handler needs the grant record or remaining
budget. It returns a truthy `Allowed(grant, remaining, reason, unjudged="")` or a
falsey `Denied(reason, would_allow, undecided=False, detail="")`.

`Denied.reason` is the refusal for the agent. `Denied.detail` holds the collected
refusals and full judge reasoning for the user. `Denied.message` joins
`brief(reason)` with `would_allow`; with no reason, it is just `would_allow`.
`Denied.explained` returns the detail when present, otherwise the reason and
remediation.

`captain_hook.grants.records.brief` takes the first sentence, strips quotation
marks and recognized record ids, replaces `ruling` with `decision`, and clips long
text at a word near 160 characters. Write `would_allow` as one short remediation
sentence. The combined block must meet `hook_lint.copy_violations`: at most two
sentences and 300 characters, with no quoted phrases, record or commit-hash-like
ids, dates, or the word `ruling` in its prose. Check the combined message;
`brief` does not enforce every copy rule or shorten `would_allow`.

For a spent approval, the agent's text names the action that used it. The grant id,
spend time, session, and agent remain in the detail. `store.unusable()` returns
`Unusable(agent, detail)` when a grant cannot spend, and `SpentError.why` carries
that value when reservation fails.

For a hook that checks several calls within one event, pass each `Proposal`
directly to `check(evt, action)`. The explicit proposal overrides the declaration's
`action` function. Such a declaration may omit `action`; calling `check(evt)` on
it without a proposal raises `TypeError`. Attachments through `hook(..., grants=...)`
still require an `action` function.

As an alternative to the `hook(...)` registration above, keep the declaration and
register this handler. It blocks check errors and uses the attachment's policy
for incomplete checks:

```python
from captain_hook import BaseHookEvent, Event, HookResult, Tool, on
from captain_hook.app import GRANTS_INCOMPLETE
from captain_hook.grants import Allowed


@on(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    only_if=[Tool("slack_reply")],
    skip_planning_agents=False,
    on_incomplete=GRANTS_INCOMPLETE,
)
def message_writes(evt: BaseHookEvent) -> HookResult:
    try:
        verdict = MESSAGE_WRITES.check(evt)
    except Exception:
        return evt.block("The grant check failed. Retry after fixing the check.")
    if isinstance(verdict, Allowed):
        return evt.context(f"Allowed by grant `{verdict.grant.id}`.")
    return evt.block(verdict.message, system_message=verdict.explained)
```

The `grants=` attachment already converts store, parse, evidence, and judge errors
inside its check to a block. Judge timeouts, backend failures, and invalid results
deny permission. A raw `check` can raise other errors; letting them escape an
ordinary handler can leave only a logged failure and no block.

Declare `judge_fails_open=True` when a judge failure should let the action through
instead. The check spends the covering grant, or mints a one-use grant on the
evidence it collected, and `Allowed.unjudged` names the failure, such as
`TimeoutError`. The minted grant asserts `standing_rules`, so a rule such as
no-broadcast still denies. The hook should show that text to the agent and log
it. A declaration whose sources collect no evidence still denies. A judge that
answers no still denies, even when a later judge call in the same check fails.
`Grants.request` records a grant only on a verdict.

`hook(..., grants=...)` sets `on_incomplete` to `captain_hook.app.GRANTS_INCOMPLETE`.
An abandoned or incomplete check blocks. The handler form above sets the same
policy explicitly.

## Manage grants from the CLI

`capt-hook grant` provides `add`, `import`, `adopt`, `spend`, `list`, `show`, and `revoke`.
Run the examples through `uvx capt-hook`, like other commands in these guides.
Replace `ROOT_SESSION_ID` with the intended root session id.

Record one approved message with a 30-minute lifetime:

```bash
uvx capt-hook grant add --kind message.write \
  --scope channel=C_EXAMPLE --scope thread=1.2 \
  --tree ROOT_SESSION_ID --uses 1 --for 30m \
  --quote 'Post the reviewed update in this thread.'
```

For `add` and `import`, repeating a scope key makes a set:
`--scope channel=C_EXAMPLE --scope channel=C_OTHER` covers either channel.
Use `--scope 'thread=*'` for any non-empty thread value; quote the asterisk so
the shell leaves it intact. These patterns share the grant's use budget.
`spend` takes the action's exact value for each key and rejects repeated keys;
it does not spend a set or expand a wildcard.

Use `--uses N` for a finite budget or `--unlimited` for a standing grant.
`--for` accepts durations such as `30m`, `8h`, or `7d`; omitting it sets no expiry.
Repeat `--rule` to assert declared rule names; `--uses` defaults to `1`.
When `--tree` is absent, the CLI reads `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, then `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID`.
Pass the root id explicitly when running from a lane.

Import a cc-notes answer using the same scope, budget, lifetime, rule, and tree
options. Replace `ANSWER_ID` with an existing answer id:

```bash
uvx capt-hook grant import ANSWER_ID --kind message.write \
  --scope channel=C_EXAMPLE --scope thread=1.2 \
  --tree ROOT_SESSION_ID --uses 1 --for 8h
```

`add` stores the quote; `import` stores the answer body and a revision key.
Neither sets an approved payload. A declaration with `ContentMatches` and a
judge therefore asks the judge about the first use.

Only the owner runs `add` and `import`, from an interactive terminal. The builtin
guard blocks agent-run Bash calls to both, and the CLI rejects noninteractive
input. Agents retry the action itself so its hook can collect the owner's evidence,
or a hook uses `Grants.request` to judge a request without spending it.

The CLI records the owner's chosen scope, budget, expiry, and tree without judging
the approval or enforcing a declaration's exact scope keys. Imported cc-notes
evidence stores the answer's revision with `live=True`, so it keeps the revision
recheck before spending. Include `Rulings` in the declaration's evidence sources
to collect that revision again.

Any agent can make a grant from another session tree usable in its own with
`capt-hook grant adopt <id> [--tree T] [--agent NAME]`. Both trees share the
grant's budget. Adopt a grant using its printed id:

```bash
uvx capt-hook grant adopt GRANT_ID --tree ROOT_SESSION_ID --agent sender
```

Omit `--tree` to adopt into the current session; `--agent` defaults to `main`.
The CLI reads the adopting session from the session environment variables even
when `--tree` is explicit. `grant show` logs each adoption with its destination
tree, timestamp, session, and agent.

An Orca lane adopts its Run coordinator's grants without a command. The builtin
`general` pack records the Orca terminal of each attended Claude session from
`ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE`, once per session. A `claude -p` session is unattended and
records nothing.

On a grants check in an Orca terminal, the framework finds the
dispatched worker for that terminal with `orca orchestration worker-list`, and reads
the Run's coordinator terminal with `orca orchestration run-show`. It then adopts
every spendable grant minted in the session tree recorded for that terminal. The
coordinator's `words`, `ask`, `spawn`, and `shell` records stay in their own tree;
automatic adoption transfers spendable grants. Each adoption is logged with
agent `orca:<run>`, so both trees share the budget, and `grant show` lists the lane.

A lane pins the coordinator session it first binds for each Run. When the coordinator
terminal's record moves to another session, the lane adopts nothing more from it.
The session re-reads the Run from Orca after one minute, or when its terminal
changes, so a finished worker stops adopting. Outside Orca, or with no recorded
coordinator session, nothing is adopted.

Inspect and revoke a grant with its printed id in place of `GRANT_ID`:

```bash
uvx capt-hook grant list --kind message.write --tree ROOT_SESSION_ID
uvx capt-hook grant list --all
uvx capt-hook grant show GRANT_ID
uvx capt-hook grant revoke GRANT_ID
```

`list` hides spent, expired, and revoked grants unless `--all` is set.
An exhausted one-use grant can still cover an identical retry within the
declaration's replay window even though it is absent from the default list.
`show` leads with the live status and remaining uses, or the reason the grant is
unusable. It then prints the record, adoptions, and every spend, including reserved,
committed, and released uses.
`revoke` prevents future spends and retries.

## Lift a session guard block

The `general` pack declares these session grant kinds:

| Kind | Scope | Action it can cover |
|------|-------|---------------------|
| `sessions.close` | `terminal=<handle>` | `orca terminal close --terminal <handle>` |
| `sessions.launchctl` | `service=<launchd label>` | `launchctl bootout`, `kickstart`, `disable`, `kill`, `stop`, or `remove` on one service |
| `sessions.task-stop` | `task=<id>` | `TaskStop`, using `task_id` or the retired `shell_id` |
| `sessions.close-settled` | Empty | `orca terminal close --terminal <handle>` for an idle, settled dispatch |
| `sessions.close.owner` | `terminal=<handle>` | A close the owner names in their words or answer |
| `sessions.launchctl.owner` | `service=<launchd label>` | A service action the owner names in their words or answer |

The first three have no judge. Their budget is one use per evidence item and
scope across all session trees, with a one-day expiry. They read
`Rulings(search=...)` for their scope value. Have the owner name it in a cc-notes
answer before the acting session starts. Inspect the spend with
`capt-hook grant show <id>`.

All three set `replay=timedelta(minutes=2)`: the same
scope and payload can reuse a committed spend for less than two minutes. This
covers the `PermissionRequest` following `PreToolUse` for the same call, or a
prompt retry. A later identical command needs new evidence.

A grant lifts a terminal close or `launchctl` stop only when the guarded call runs
once. It must be the first command at top level, and the Bash payload text must
start with it. Every other command must be a pipe successor, so
`launchctl kickstart -k system/com.example.orca-serve 2>&1 | tail -3` can qualify.
Loops, `&&` or `;` chains such as `cd /tmp && launchctl ...`, background `&`,
`sh -c`, substitutions, and commands respelled through variables keep the block.
`TaskStop` is a tool call and runs once by construction.

The root session's `TaskStop` is never guarded, so `sessions.task-stop` only
lifts a stop from a subagent or an Orca lane.

For `launchctl`, spell the command and target literally, without wrappers,
substitutions, or variables. Service targets are `system/<label>` or
`<domain>/<id>/<label>`, where the domain is `gui`, `user`, `pid`, or `login`.
`kill` takes a signal before the target; `stop` and `remove` also accept a bare
label. No lift covers domain targets such as `gui/501`, the `reboot`, `asuser`,
`bsexec`, or `unload` verbs, or any other session-guard block.

`sessions.task-stop` also accepts live `OwnTeammate` evidence. The task id must
match `<name>@session-<8 hex>`. On `PostToolUse`, the general pack records an
`Agent` or `Task` result with `status: teammate_spawned` and its `teammate_id`
as a `spawn` record keyed to the spawning session and agent. `OwnTeammate` reads
that record first, so compaction does not erase the proof. Without a record, it
looks for the matching result in this agent's own transcript.

A matching spawn grants one deterministic use. The team id comes from the Claude
process's session id at spawn; after a resume it can differ from the hook payload's
session id. Bare teammate ids do not qualify. A lane cannot use its sibling's or
root's spawn record.

`OwnShell` gives the same one-use lift for a background shell this agent started.
The pack records a Bash result's non-empty `backgroundTaskId` as a `shell` record
on `PostToolUse`. `TaskStop` must name that task id, and the record must belong to
the calling session and agent. Both child record kinds stay in their own tree
during coordinator adoption. These lifts share the two-minute identical-retry
window of `sessions.task-stop`.

`sessions.close` also accepts live `CreatedHere` evidence when all checks pass:

- This session's transcript shows `orca terminal create` as the only command in
  its Bash call. It must use bare `orca` without an environment prefix or
  substitution. `./orca` and other paths do not qualify. Its JSON output must name
  `result.terminal.handle`. Alternatively, an `orca-launch.sh <lane> ...` call must
  output `terminal=<handle>` and have a matching
  `~/.claude/scratch/orca-launch/*/<lane>.terminal.json` receipt dated by mtime
  between call start minus one second and result plus one second.
- `orca orchestration worker-list` names no dispatch for the terminal across any
  Run, with `ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE` unset for the probe.
- `orca terminal wait --for tui-idle` succeeds within one second; the screen
  shows Claude's `❯` or Codex's `› Ask Codex to do anything` prompt among its last
  eight nonblank, non-border lines, with no busy marker. The last spoken line
  before the prompt must not end in `?`.

Stored grants based on `CreatedHere` recheck this evidence, so a busy terminal
loses that coverage. An owner ruling is a separate lift and does not require these
creation and idle checks. A terminal whose process tree has no agent can close
directly. Name one literal terminal; batches stay blocked. `--tab` requires
`orca terminal list --include-visual-layouts` to prove the terminal is alone in
its tab; otherwise, the denial says to drop `--tab`.

After `sessions.close` denies, `sessions.close-settled` can lift a close when the
terminal's process tree is readable, `orca orchestration worker-list` records its
`dispatchStatus` as `completed` or `failed`, and it passes the idle checks above.
The caller must be the root session coordinating the dispatch's Run. The hook
event has no `agent_id`, and the request's `ORCA_TERMINAL_HANDLE` is set and matches
`result.run.coordinator_handle` from
`orca orchestration run-show --id <runId> --json`, using the worker row's `runId`.
Other terminal lanes, in-process teammates, callers outside Orca, and another
Run's coordinator get no lift.

The grants `Judge` uses capt-hook's small model to decide whether a standing owner
ruling covers the terminal's Orca record. The proposal's payload names the Run;
its summary identifies the caller as the Run's coordinator. After the judge
allows, the guard re-reads the worker row and idle prompt. The same dispatch must
still hold the terminal as `completed` or `failed`, and the agent must still be
idle. Otherwise, the guard blocks the close, releases the reserved spend, and
sets `systemMessage` to
`sessions: the terminal's dispatch or idle prompt changed while the judge decided.`

`StandingRulings` reads cc-notes answers `c9b27c1` for settled-dispatch cleanup and
`6190a4a` for failed-launch orphans by id with `ccn answer show`. Only answers last
written before the acting session started count; each stays pinned to its live
revision. A missing answer (exit 3) supplies no evidence. The grant has empty
scope, unlimited uses, and no expiry; the judge checks each close again. Live or
unsettled dispatches, busy agents, terminals without a dispatch, unreadable
process trees, loops, and batches do not qualify for this lift.

Its remediation is: "Close only an idle terminal whose dispatch Orca records as
settled, under a standing owner decision recorded in cc-notes before the closing
session."

The `.owner` kinds try the owner's current words after the existing cc-notes,
created-here and settled-dispatch lifts. Only the
spawning root qualifies: the event has no `agent_id` and `evt.ctx.root_path` is
`None`. A teammate or a session with a root transcript gets no owner-named lift.

`OwnerNaming` collects prompts, human-queued messages, and `AskUserQuestion`
answers that name the exact terminal handle or service label. Matching includes the
question and option context, so the owner can select an option that names the
target. With no naming evidence, the hook makes no judge call.

The judge applies `OWNER_NAMED_RULES`: the words must ask to close, stop, restart,
or kick that target, or choose an option that does. A description, a general
cleanup request, or words naming another target do not authorize it. These
declarations default to a one-use mint budget and a one-hour expiry, with a
two-minute identical-retry window. The command-shape restrictions above still apply.

The sessions guard does not block `orca-gc --run <run> [--dispatch <ctx>]`.

The owner can mint one close from a terminal; replace the placeholders:

```bash
uvx capt-hook grant add --kind sessions.close --scope terminal=TERMINAL_HANDLE \
  --tree ROOT_SESSION_ID --for 1d --quote 'Close TERMINAL_HANDLE once.'
```

Denials give the agent the short refusal and remedy when a grant check supplies a
reason. The full detail reaches the user in `systemMessage`, with the session
check prefixed by `sessions: `. With no reason, the guard keeps its own block text.

## Test grants inline

Seed a real grant store with `Input(grants=[...])`. Each test starts with an empty,
isolated store, then loads its own seeds. Match the input's `session_id` to the
grant's `tree`. The model stub defaults to `allow=False`; use `llm` to exercise
an allow, its reason, cited evidence, or a `standing` quote.

This complete hook tests a report write with no grant, an exact approved payload,
a rejected change, and a change the judge allows. Save it in
`.claude/hooks/report_grants.py`:

```python
from datetime import UTC, datetime

from captain_hook import (
    BaseHookEvent, Block, ContentMatches, Event, Grant, Grants, Input,
    Judge, Proposal, Tool, Warn, hook,
)
from captain_hook.grants import Evidence


def report_action(evt: BaseHookEvent) -> Proposal:
    raw = evt.input.raw
    return Proposal(
        scope={"path": raw["file_path"]},
        payload={"content": raw["content"]},
        summary=f"write {raw['file_path']}",
    )


REPORT_WRITES = Grants(
    "report.write",
    scope=("path",),
    action=report_action,
    rules=(ContentMatches(text=("content",)),),
    judge=Judge("Require the owner's approval for this report's content."),
)
APPROVED = Grant(
    id="0123456789ab",
    kind="report.write",
    tree="example-root",
    scope={"path": "/tmp/report.txt"},
    approved={"content": "Reviewed report"},
    evidence=[Evidence(id="words:review", source="words", quote="Write the reviewed report.")],
    author="test",
    created=datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC),
)

hook(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    "Report writes need permission. Ask the user to approve the report.",
    only_if=[Tool("Write")],
    block=True,
    grants=REPORT_WRITES,
    tests={
        Input(file="/tmp/report.txt", content="Reviewed report", session_id="example-root"): Block(),
        Input(
            file="/tmp/report.txt", content="Reviewed report",
            session_id="example-root", grants=[APPROVED],
        ): Warn(pattern="allowed by grant `0123456789ab`, 0 use"),
        Input(
            file="/tmp/report.txt", content="Changed report",
            session_id="example-root", grants=[APPROVED],
        ): Block(pattern="inline test stub", system_message="inline test stub"),
        Input(
            file="/tmp/report.txt", content="Changed report",
            session_id="example-root", grants=[APPROVED],
            llm={"allow": True, "reason": "The owner approved the revision.", "relied_on": ["words:review"]},
        ): Warn(pattern="allowed by grant `0123456789ab`"),
    },
)
```

Run the inline tests:

```bash
uvx capt-hook test
```

An attached grant's allow returns a context note, so its inline expectation is
`Warn`, even though the hook lifts its block. A `standing` override needs matching
owner words from an evidence provider. Include `uses` in the `llm` override for a
counted grant; leaving it unset on a standing approval allows unlimited uses.
Use `scope` to test widening and `refusal` to check the agent-facing message.
Inline stubs test the declaration and verdict handling. They do not test whether
the model interprets permission correctly.
